options.text: Enforces rules on resource configurations (audit, deny, or remediate)
Controls which users can sign in to Azure

questions.explanation: Azure Policy enforces organizational rules on how resources are configured — it can audit, deny non-compliant creates, or remediate. (RBAC governs who can act; Policy governs how resources are configured.)

questions.prompt: Which are legitimate ways to reduce Azure spend? Select all that apply.

options.text: Right-size resources and shut down idle ones
Buy reservations or savings plans for steady workloads
Use Azure Hybrid Benefit to reuse existing licenses

questions.explanation: Right-sizing, reservations/savings plans, and Hybrid Benefit all cut cost. Azure Advisor's recommendations should be used, not ignored.

questions.prompt: The resource lock type that lets you read and modify a resource but not delete it is ____.
questions.explanation: A CanNotDelete lock allows reading and modifying but prevents deletion — ideal for protecting critical resources like a production database.

items.text: Track actual spend in Cost Management
Set a budget with a threshold
Get alerted as you approach it

questions.explanation: Estimate up front, track real spend, set budgets, and receive alerts before you overspend.

questions.prompt: Match each governance tool to its role.
questions.explanation: Policy enforces config rules; locks protect resources; budgets watch spend; management groups scale governance across subscriptions.
